#5223. Stellar Foundation Backs Marketnode to Expand Tokenized Funds Across Asia-Pacific

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: The Stellar Development Foundation announced a strategic investment in Marketnode on October 29, aiming to widen institutional access to tokenized investment products in Asia-Pacific. Marketnode is backed by Euroclear, HSBC, SGX Group and Temasek, but the announcement did not disclose an investment amount or ownership percentage.

Tokenization is frequently described as a technology that makes financial assets available on a blockchain. The harder part is often distribution: who is allowed to buy the product, how ownership is recorded, and which regulated institutions can service it.

That is the focus of a Stellar Development Foundation investment announced October 29. The foundation said it had made a strategic investment in Marketnode, an Asia-Pacific digital-market-infrastructure company with backing from Euroclear, HSBC, SGX Group and Temasek.

Marketnode works with funds, credit products and structured investments, supplying technology and services for issuance, distribution and ongoing servicing. The ambition is to connect the firms that originate investment products with distributors and eligible investors using blockchain rails where appropriate.

A token representing a fund interest does not necessarily make that fund available to anyone with a wallet. Eligibility requirements, investor onboarding, local laws, transfer restrictions and redemption arrangements still apply. In institutional markets, making those controls work is often the difference between an experiment and a product that can be distributed at scale.

The announcement says Marketnode has already worked with global and regional asset managers and has discussed onchain access to select BNY Investments funds on Stellar. It also identifies relationships with asset managers including Franklin Templeton, Maybank Asset Management, CGS International and WisdomTree.

Those references are evidence of an existing institutional network, but they should not be read as a guarantee that every product from every named organisation is universally available or that all its assets have migrated to Stellar.

The region contains large financial centres, significant cross-border investment activity and a range of approaches to regulated digital assets. A platform that can coordinate issuance and distribution may lower some operational friction between asset managers, custodians and investors.

Still, a public blockchain can supply only part of the solution. Legal title, disclosure, investor protections, tax reporting and reconciliation with traditional securities systems remain essential. Marketnode’s experience with institutional processes may be as important to the foundation’s plans as the underlying Stellar network itself.

For comparison, NewsBTC has covered the NYSE’s plans for tokenized-securities infrastructure. Tokenization and settlement are related pieces of a wider market-infrastructure problem, and both must fit the compliance standards that institutions already face.

Neither the monetary value of the investment nor the stake acquired was specified in the foundation’s announcement. That limits any attempt to infer Marketnode’s valuation or measure how much capital Stellar is committing relative to its other ecosystem investments.

There is also a difference between financial backing and market adoption. An investment can help a company build integrations, expand teams or develop products, but proof of use will come from assets actually issued, transactions settled, and institutions actively servicing customers over time.

The next useful milestones would include disclosed product launches, participating financial institutions, client access arrangements and measurable volume. Stellar has identified a credible institutional distribution problem and is backing a company that works on it. How much of that infrastructure eventually runs through its network remains the question to watch.

Bitcoin snapped a seven-week holding above the 50-week moving average (MA) with a weekly close at $74,968. According to the latest Galaxy Research report, BTC settled 0.7% under this key line, which now sits at $75,488.

Alex Thorn, the firm’s head of research, calls it a fakeout. The history is on his side: it's standard Bitcoin mechanics to slip back under the 50-week MA right after a bear-market bottom, and it's what shapes the structure of the four-year cycle. It has happened exactly twice before.

Losing the trendline again right after reclaiming it is how the biggest cryptocurrency has always behaved. Previous cycles played out like this:

The current chart is running the same script. From the $123,524 peak in October 2025, the coin bled 51.8% into the June cycle bottom at $59,517. A rebound then shoved the price back above the 50-week MA at $81,195. Today’s price is 7.7% off that September reclaim level, yet Bitcoin maintains a comfortable 26% cushion above the June bottom.

Thorn isn’t selling certainty. Two cycles is a thin sample, and bottoms only get confirmed in the rearview mirror. The margin for error is wide: in 2012, Bitcoin broke down again from 18% above the line, while in 2015 it held from just 8% above.

“Bitcoin just closed below its 50 week moving average after holding above it for 7 consecutive weeks. Two other times (2011-12 & 2019-20) btc closed below its 50w after reclaiming its post-bear bottom. Neither of those times did the bear make a new lower low (weekly close data),” the analyst notes.

One level kills the bull case for this 4-year cycle: $59,517. Galaxy Research says on-chain metrics, whale positioning and market sentiment all point to a consolidation that is technically ripe for stacking on spot. The technical case stays alive as long as Bitcoin reclaims the 50-week MA and holds it within the next month.

#5221. Bitcoin Slides to $73,510 Over the Weekend: Did Nvidia Scandal Trigger BTC’s $2,000 Flash Crash?

Bitcoin news: BTC fell to $73,510 on Sunday, 100 minutes after the Nvidia scandal broke. Thin weekend trading let the drop run further.

In Bitcoin news overnight, BTC USD price fell from $75,607 to $73,510 in ten minutes on Sunday evening, its lowest price since August 21. The worst of it came at 21:55 UTC, or 4:55 p.m. in New York. In that single minute, Bitcoin dropped 1.9% on Binance.

Most traders blamed Nvidia. Earlier that afternoon, CNBC reported that Nvidia’s board had opened an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believe was passing information to Beijing (it’s just speculation for now).

Huang admitted the affair in an email to staff.

After Jensen Huang admitted having an affair, a whale opened a 10x short on 30,000 $NVDA ($5.44M) on Hyperliquid.https://t.co/RztJx5FNge pic.twitter.com/zuyV2K0ftN

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 9, 2026

The bounce since then has been small. BTC traded at $74,184 on Binance on Monday morning, 2.2% below where it stood when the Nvidia story broke. The drop also marked a fifth straight losing week: the weekly candle closed at $74,851, below the week’s open of $78,354.

So did the Nvidia scandal really trigger the dump, or did thin weekend trading turn an ordinary sell-off into a sharp one?

Discover: Sam Altman ChatGPT AI Predicts an Insane Move for Cardano (ADA)

The timing does not fit a straight reaction to the news. CNBC published its report at 3:12 p.m. Eastern time on Sunday, which is 20:12 UTC. Bitcoin traded at $75,880 on Binance in that minute. For the next 90 minutes, almost nothing happened. At 21:44 UTC, BTC sat at $75,607, just 0.4% lower than when the story appeared.

Then the selling started, and it started in Ethereum. Between 21:50 and 21:55 UTC, ETH fell 6.9% on Binance, from $2,213 to $2,060. Bitcoin fell 2.4% over the same five minutes.

That pattern points to a liquidation cascade, a chain of forced sales. Traders who borrow to bet on higher prices get their positions force-closed when the price falls past a set point. Each forced sale pushes the price down to the next group of bets.

BREAKING: $1,000,000,000 liquidated from the crypto market in the past 10 minutes.$BTC falls under $74,000$ETH falls under $2,125$XRP falls under $1.10 $SOL falls under $90 pic.twitter.com/hIZhzQFJJe

— Watcher.Guru (@WatcherGuru) November 8, 2026

The news still mattered. Nvidia is the biggest AI stock, and Bitcoin has traded in step with AI shares for weeks: Thursday’s chip-stock sell-off is what pushed BTC below its 200-day average. With stock markets closed, crypto was the only market open to sell into the headline.

A second headline added to the Bitcoin news mood. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called Iran’s demands “outrageous” and said talks had made no progress.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

Weekend trading explains why the drop went so far. Over the past year, about $24 million of BTC changed hands on Binance in a typical weekend hour, half the $48 million in a typical weekday hour.

We checked every hour in that year in which Bitcoin fell at least 2.5% below the hour’s opening price. There were 29 of them.

Sunday’s drop came with $180 million of trading in the hour. That is the second-lowest of all 29, and about half the median of $366 million.

In other words, it took less selling than usual to move the price this far. The busiest minute, 21:55 UTC, traded $75 million of BTC on Binance, about three times what changes hands in a whole weekend hour.

Weekends do not cause more crashes, though. Only 6 of the 29 drops came on a Saturday or Sunday, slightly fewer than the 29% of all hours that fall on weekends. What a quiet weekend changes is how far the price moves for each dollar sold.

One note: much of the forced selling happens in futures markets, which this count does not include.

So both played a part. Nvidia and Iran gave traders a reason to cut risk, and thin weekend trading let the selling run further than it would on a weekday.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

It held on the first test. BTC bounced to $75,735 within two hours of the low, but it has slipped back to $74,184, and the daily chart still leans lower.

Bitcoin trades below all three of its daily exponential moving averages (EMAs), trend lines that give recent prices more weight. It lost the 200-day EMA, which tracks the long-term trend, on Thursday.

For traders following Bitcoin news this week, Monday’s stock market open is the next test. It is the first chance for Nvidia shares to trade on the news, eight days before the company reports earnings on November 17.

The US Treasury has added eight Canada-based money services businesses to its sanctions list, alleging that they helped move value for the Iranian regime and sanctioned actors. The November 6 action explicitly focuses on exchanges between local currencies and digital assets, demonstrating how crypto compliance disputes can arise at the point where cash, informal transfer networks and onchain wallets intersect. It is a targeted designation, not a claim that ordinary Canadian remittances are inherently suspect.

The Office of Foreign Assets Control says the companies enabled conversion of Iranian rials and other currencies into digital assets used for cross-border payments. Several allegedly handled transactions linked to sanctioned Iranian crypto exchangers or wallet addresses associated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Treasury also says some had changed names or addresses while remaining active. These are allegations and designations by US authorities; the release does not supply a separate court finding against every transaction. The policy rationale is to disrupt businesses officials believe provide a bridge from restricted counterparties to otherwise reachable financial channels.

OFAC designations can trigger obligations for US persons and firms subject to US jurisdiction, including blocking relevant property and avoiding prohibited dealings. Separately, exchanges, stablecoin issuers and payment companies may reassess exposure to identified counterparties. The official listing includes several Tron addresses, which may assist screening, but crypto enforcement cannot be reduced to one blockchain. A listed firm can change the addresses it uses, and a matching transaction must still be interpreted in its legal and operational context. Readers should distinguish a prohibited counterparty relationship from an unproven allegation about an unrelated user of the same network.

Canada has established money service businesses handling remittances and currency exchange, including legitimate cross-border commerce. Treasury argues that particular operators were used to facilitate sanctioned Iranian flows. This creates a practical challenge for compliance teams: the business model of moving small international payments is not itself an indication of sanctions evasion. Screening requires understanding the firm, beneficial ownership, customer relationships and transaction patterns. A wallet-address match is useful evidence but cannot replace that broader inquiry, especially when a transaction passes through several custodians or payment processors.

The same day Treasury announced a separate FinCEN order restricting US institutional transfers to and from MEXC Global. The two announcements form part of Operation Economic Outcast, but they use different legal tools. Here, OFAC has designated specific businesses; in the exchange case, FinCEN is restricting financial transfers involving a named platform. Conflating the mechanisms would lead to confused headlines about who may transact and what happens next. The financial impact also depends on whether designated businesses have US-linked property, correspondent relationships or other reachable assets.

The official OFAC list, including aliases and any later amendments, should be the reference point for compliance decisions. Investigators may publish additional evidence or update designations; businesses concerned about exposure need qualified legal advice rather than acting on social-media summaries. For the crypto sector, the larger story is the growing willingness of authorities to look past the chain itself and act against money movement businesses that turn digital assets into usable payment routes.

TL;DR: Global crypto compliance rules may face a tougher practical test after the Financial Action Task Force agreed to review jurisdictions with longstanding shortcomings in virtual asset oversight. In a November 6 readout, the US Treasury said the review would identify decisions for the next FATF plenary.

Global crypto compliance rules may face a tougher practical test after the Financial Action Task Force agreed to review jurisdictions with longstanding shortcomings in virtual asset oversight. In a November 6 readout, the US Treasury said the review would identify decisions for the next FATF plenary. The announcement is procedural, but it points toward a shift from writing standards to asking whether countries are actually implementing them.

According to Treasury, FATF plans a targeted examination of countries whose persistent weaknesses in virtual asset regulation create financial crime risks. The group also adopted mutual evaluation reports of the United States and Mexico and advanced work on scam centers. A targeted review is not itself a new global cryptocurrency prohibition, nor does it publicly name a complete roster of jurisdictions that will be penalized. The key next milestone is the group's discussion of potential accountability measures at a later plenary. Until then, claims that FATF has already imposed a particular sanction would go beyond the published outcome.

Many businesses now serve customers across several jurisdictions through one front end, while settlement takes place on public blockchains. Rules on customer identification, beneficial ownership, suspicious activity reporting and the information that accompanies transfers differ in implementation even where international standards are broadly similar. That creates opportunities for regulatory arbitrage: a risky intermediary can seek a location with weak supervision while accessing liquidity elsewhere. FATF's concern is not that moving value onchain is automatically criminal. It is that supervision of the companies facilitating that movement can lag behind the reach of their services.

The plenary also considered financial flows supporting scam compounds and reiterated concerns about Iran-related illicit finance. That matters because the same laundering networks can involve conventional banks, shell companies, money service businesses and crypto assets. A credible enforcement strategy must examine all these links rather than assume a blockchain transaction tells the whole story. Treasury's account suggests policymakers increasingly see digital asset compliance as one part of wider cross-border financial intelligence, not an isolated regulatory category.

Exchanges and custody businesses should watch for the full FATF plenary outcomes, the scope of any jurisdiction review and subsequent national rulemaking. Investors should be cautious about treating an international standards discussion as an immediate trigger for price moves. The significance is slower-moving: countries with persistent gaps may face added scrutiny, and market participants could eventually find that familiar customer flows require more verification, more data exchange or different service arrangements.

As expected, this has prompted a question: Is altcoin season now off the radar in 2026?

Alphractal analysis shows that around August to October 2026, both Bitcoin’s 60-day return and the median altcoin’s return climbed to roughly +50-60%, with altcoins moving in sync. But, by November, both lines have dropped back to roughly 0%, and the median altcoin sits slightly below Bitcoin.

#5212. Keno RTP by Number of Picks: What Changes and What Doesn’t

Home » Crypto Market News » Keno RTP by Number of Picks: What Changes and What Doesn’t

This article explores how keno pick counts affect RTP, hit frequency, and volatility. Using probability calculations and simulated sessions, it shows why more numbers do not necessarily mean better returns, and how paytable structure determines your long-term expected payout.

Ask keno players which pick count “pays best” and you get strong opinions: one or two numbers for steady hits, ten for the big multipliers. Both camps are usually arguing about the wrong thing.

Return to player, or RTP, is the share of every dollar wagered that a game pays back over the long run. In keno, that figure is set by the paytable, and each pick count has its own paytable. So the honest answer to “which pick count has the best RTP” depends entirely on how those tables were built. On a modern crypto board, the answer is often “none of them,” and the more useful question becomes what the pick count does to everything else.

Below, the math runs on a 40-number board that draws 10, using openly published paytables plus a few hypothetical edits. Probabilities are exact; session figures come from 20,000 simulated runs.

Traditional casino keno uses an 80-number board with 20 numbers drawn. Each spot count gets its own paytable, and operators calibrate each one separately. Published estimates put the house edge in land-based keno somewhere between 20% and 40%, and it can shift by several points from one spot count to the next. That is why old guides compare 4-spot and 7-spot tickets so closely.

Online and crypto versions changed the design brief. Many operators now publish a single RTP for the whole game and then build every pick count’s paytable to land on that number. When that is the case, the pick count stops being a lever on expected return. A well-run bitcoin casino keno table that advertises 98% should return close to 98% whether you pick one number or ten. Rounding multipliers to one decimal means no table hits its target exactly.

Before any paytable comes into it, the board itself fixes the odds. With 40 numbers and 10 drawn, each number you pick has a 1 in 4 chance of landing. Your average number of hits is simply your pick count divided by four: 0.25 hits on one pick, 1.25 on five, 2.5 on ten.

The chance of catching at least one number climbs fast as you add picks:

The chance of hitting every number you picked collapses even faster. One pick is 1 in 4. Five picks is 1 in 2,611. Ten picks is 1 in 847,660,528. None of this says anything about RTP yet. RTP is the sum of probability times payout across every paytable row.

Here is what that sum gives for three paytables published on a live bitcoin keno page that states a 98% RTP:

The spread between them is 0.04 percentage points. Over $10,000 of total wagers, that is a difference of about four dollars in expected return. Pick count and risk setting do not move RTP here; the gap to 98% is rounding.

The same arithmetic tells you what a fair one-pick table would look like. One pick hits 25% of the time, so a 98% table has to pay 3.92x on a hit. If a one-pick ticket somewhere pays 3x instead, it returns 75%.

If RTP stays flat, pick count changes two things: how often you get paid and how hard the balance swings.

That last line is the surprise. Five picks on this table is almost nine times as swingy as ten picks on Low, even though both return the same 98 cents per dollar. More picks does not mean more volatility; the paytable’s shape decides it.

Breaking each table’s return down row by row shows where the money comes from.

On ten picks at Low risk, the 2-, 3- and 4-hit rows deliver about 90% of the entire return. The 1,000x prize for ten hits contributes roughly 0.0001 cents per dollar, close enough to zero that removing it would not change the RTP at the second decimal. Medium risk on ten picks moves the weight up a little: the 3- and 4-hit rows carry 74%, and the 5-hit row adds another 17%.

Five picks is different. The 2-hit row carries 42.5% of the return and the 3-hit row 34%, but the 300x prize for five hits carries 11.7% on its own, the same share as the 12x row below it. On a five-pick bitcoin keno game, the top prize is a real part of what you are being paid back. On ten picks, it is decoration.

Knowing which rows carry the return shows where a stingy operator could cut quietly. Two hypothetical edits:

On ten picks at Low risk, cutting the 2-hit payout from 1.1x to 1.0x would lower RTP by 3.1 percentage points, from about 98% to about 95%. Halving the 1,000x top prize to 500x would lower it by less than one ten-thousandth of a point. The jackpot is the row players look at, and the one that barely matters.

On five picks, the picture flips. Halving the 300x prize to 150x would cost 5.7 points of RTP, which is more than the 2.8 points lost by trimming the 2-hit row from 1.5x to 1.4x. So for high counts, check the small rows; for low and middle counts, check the top prize too.

Here is 500 rounds at $1, across 20,000 simulated sessions per table. Expected loss in every case is about $10.

Same RTP, very different evenings. Five picks on Low produces the worst typical session and the best lucky one, because so much of its return sits in a prize that turns up once every 2,611 rounds on average. Ten picks on Low is the slow grind. With crypto keno, where a round settles in seconds, 500 rounds can pass quickly, so choose the session shape you want before starting.

Check that your probabilities sum to 1 before trusting the answer. If totals across pick counts differ by more than a few tenths of a point, some counts are priced worse; avoid those.

On provably fair games, you can also verify each draw against the published seeds.

To see how the published paytables look in practice, you can try keno at Jacks Club and run the spreadsheet check against the tables shown on the game page. The numbers should agree to within rounding.

Keno is a game of chance, and no pick count changes the long-run edge. Play only with money you can afford to lose. 18+ only; check that online gambling is legal where you live.

TL;DR: US officials are pursuing the corporate structures behind online investment scams, not merely the wallets receiving stolen funds. On November 5, Treasury sanctioned four individuals and 41 entities it says supported the Prince Group transnational criminal organization, alongside an individual accused of managing another scam network.

US officials are pursuing the corporate structures behind online investment scams, not merely the wallets receiving stolen funds. On November 5, Treasury sanctioned four individuals and 41 entities it says supported the Prince Group transnational criminal organization, alongside an individual accused of managing another scam network. The action links alleged digital asset fraud to offshore companies, nominee ownership and payment facilitators, showing why tracking a suspicious transaction is only one part of the investigative work.

Treasury says the newly designated individuals and companies helped preserve business networks linked to Prince Group after previous sanctions in 2025 and 2026. Some allegedly managed offshore entities, concealed beneficial ownership or provided services to executives already designated. The agency also named a Malaysian individual it says operated a network of scammers based in Madagascar. These are official allegations contained in a sanctions announcement. The release is not a determination that every customer or employee associated with a named commercial organization participated in a scam.

Treasury describes digital asset investment fraud, romance scams and other online deception that persuaded victims to transfer funds to accounts controlled by criminals. Some operations involved Southeast Asian compounds and people coerced or trafficked into carrying out fraud. Payments can begin in banks or payment apps before reaching exchanges and wallets. That chain of movement is why a case presented as a cryptocurrency scandal may also depend on property companies, corporate agents and conventional commercial intermediaries. Focusing only on one wallet address risks missing the structures that allow a network to reappear.

Sanctions can restrict dealings with named entities, but investigators often need to look at people who control firms behind layers of holding companies. Treasury alleges that associates transferred property, managed businesses and obscured who benefited from revenue after earlier designations. Beneficial ownership checks are therefore relevant to exchanges and crypto businesses alongside blockchain analytics. A business might see no direct transfer with a known illicit wallet yet still have a serious counterparty problem if a customer or supplier is controlled by a sanctioned person.

The announcement credits law enforcement and overseas authorities, including British Virgin Islands and UK partners. Such cooperation helps connect financial accounts, registrations and corporate directors with onchain evidence. It also illustrates a limit of public blockchain transparency: address-level visibility cannot necessarily tell investigators who arranged a business structure or which employee authorized an account. Effective disruption tends to require both digital tracing and traditional records. The announced designations may also affect innocent customers of related services, making accurate identification particularly important.

Victims of online investment fraud should preserve transaction identifiers, messages and platform information and report them to official authorities, rather than paying third parties that promise guaranteed fund recovery. For businesses, the immediate question is whether any listed counterparty, alias or beneficial owner appears in existing relationships. The broader lesson is that crypto-enabled scams are an organized financial crime problem with a real-world corporate infrastructure, and enforcement is increasingly directed at that infrastructure.

XRP Ledger co-creator David Schwartz dropped his $1.7 million tax bill on X to settle a long-running fight over the token’s value. Ripple’s CTO Emeritus was swatting away haters who accused him of dumping XRP on the market. One commenter called XRP “a terrible investment,” adding that nobody would blame the engineer for heading for the exit. Schwartz kept it short: “The $1.7 million I paid in capital gains tax says otherwise.”

In 2025, Schwartz sold about 2.5 million XRP, according to his own words. Nearly all of it came from bonuses for his work in 2020 and 2023. Posting the numbers was no accident. Schwartz is killing rumors about what Ripple’s "big guns" really pocket and proving he has nothing to hide.

The sale is one chapter in a bigger personal saga Schwartz has been unpacking piece by piece from 2024 through 2026. At his peak he held around 26 million XRP. By August 2026, that stack had shrunk to just 2 million. Describing the 92% drawdown, he chose his words carefully: “I think I’m down from about 26 million at my peak to about 2 million now.”

Some went out as gifts and transfers, but he sold most of it on the open market.

He started taking profits the moment the price touched $0.10. Schwartz admits he never believed the coin would break $0.25. The same paranoia made him dump his entire 40,000 ETH position at a measly $1.05 apiece.

“Obviously, I wish I hadn’t done those things,” the developer says of the billions he left on the table.

Schwartz opposes the approach many attribute to as "diamond hands". He openly says he “really, really hates risk” and doesn’t count himself among long-term holders. He and his wife had an ironclad rule to sell a fixed slice of their holdings every time the price printed a new all-time high. Cashing out is simply the cost of being able to “sleep better at night.” These days, volatility barely touches him as his net worth is now largely cut loose from price swings.

Based on his own admission, Schwartz moved most of his savings into Ripple stock. The shares are illiquid, sure, but they give direct exposure to the tech giant’s wins and fully insulate his personal capital from exchange chaos.

#5207. 2026 XRP Rich-List Thresholds Fall Sharply From 2020

Home » Ripple (XRP) » 2026 XRP Rich-List Thresholds Fall Sharply From 2020

The accounts multiplied, adding lower-percentage cut-offs required to land in any fixed-percentage tier.

The amount of XRP tokens needed to rank in the upper tiers of the XRP rich-list has dropped significantly over the past six years.

A comparison of snapshots from July 2020 and early November 2026 shows lower entry points across major percentiles, even as the number of funded accounts has climbed past 8.3 million.

The most commonly cited threshold tells a clear story. In July 2020, an account needed roughly 80,033 XRP to enter the top 1%. By November 6, 2026, that figure had fallen to about 43,313 XRP.

Similar XRP rich-list declines appear at other levels: the top 0.01% entry dropped from around 24.2 million XRP to roughly 3.6 million, while the top 0.1% moved from about 750,000 XRP to nearly 271,000.

Lower tiers followed a very similar pattern. The top 0.5% requirement fell from approximately 150,000 XRP to 78,000, the top 5% from about 10,400 to 7,200, and the top 10% from roughly 3,000 XRP to just over 2,000.

🚨XRP RICH LIST JUST UPDATED!!! 🤑 TOP 4% = 10,000 XRP!🚨Top 1% = 43,301 XRPTop 4% = 10,003 XRPTop 10% = 2,056 XRP Are you $XRP Rich?👁🤑#XRP #Ripple #BTC #Altcoins #Crypto pic.twitter.com/RfIwFPsMOq

Recent live trackers place the top 1% cutoff in a similar range, confirming the broader downward shift as the account base expands.

The decline coincides with steady growth in funded accounts on the XRP Ledger. The network now exceeds 8.3 million accounts, a substantial increase from earlier years.

Adding large numbers of smaller accounts mathematically lowers the balance required to land in any fixed percentage tier, even if existing large holders do not sell.

Most accounts still hold relatively little; the median balance remains in the low tens of XRP, and a large majority sit well below 1,000 XRP.

This XRP rich-list expansion has increased the absolute number of accounts that qualify for higher percentiles. The top 1% now includes tens of thousands more addresses than it did a few years ago, simply because the total base is larger.

Raw account rankings do not map cleanly to individual holders. Many people maintain multiple wallets, and a single exchange address can represent thousands of customers. One observer noted holding roughly a dozen XRP wallets personally.

I have about 10 XRP wallets. Yep, many holders have many so yeah there is that.

Exchange and institutional addresses dominate the very top of the list, so concentration figures that treat every account as a separate person overstate how widely the supply is held by retail.

Ripple-linked accounts and major exchanges continue to control large portions of the supply, including substantial amounts held in escrow.

These structural features mean the falling percentile thresholds reflect both genuine growth in the number of accounts and the persistent weight of large custodial and institutional balances.

The lower entry points make certain ranking milestones more accessible in pure XRP terms than they were in 2020. At the same time, the data does not indicate that large holders have broadly distributed their tokens or that overall concentration at the top has disappeared.

The XRP rich-list comparison offers a clear view of how the XRP Ledger’s account base and balance distribution have changed over six years. It remains a snapshot of addresses, not a direct count of individual investors or a forecast of future price action.

#5206. SEC Staff Gives Canton Coin No-Action Relief, but the Conditions Matter

TL;DR: Canton Coin received an important piece of US regulatory clarity on November 3 when staff in the Securities and Exchange Commission's Division of Corporation Finance issued a no-action response. The staff said, based on representations made to it, that Canton Coin fits the description of a digital commodity in the Commission's March interpretation.

Canton Coin received an important piece of US regulatory clarity on November 3 when staff in the Securities and Exchange Commission's Division of Corporation Finance issued a no-action response. The staff said, based on representations made to it, that Canton Coin fits the description of a digital commodity in the Commission's March interpretation. That is meaningful for network participants, but the letter is narrower than a general exemption for every token on Canton or every method of selling cryptocurrency.

The response considers the network's claimed absence of a central controlling party and the connection between the token's value and the programmatic operation of the network. It also addresses the minting of Canton Coin by super validators, validators and application providers under the arrangements described in the applicant's letter. On that basis, staff said it would not recommend enforcement action for the specified minting without registration under the cited Securities Act and Exchange Act provisions. Importantly, the response is expressed as a staff position on enforcement recommendations, not a court ruling or a Commission-wide legal declaration.

The letter relies on representations that network participants receive tokens for operating infrastructure or providing applications, rather than expecting profits primarily from a central manager's efforts. It also depends on the network being operational and decentralized in the way described. Those facts are not mere decoration. The letter expressly cautions that different circumstances could lead staff to a different conclusion. A token issuer with a presale, centralized discretion or a different rewards model should not assume the same analysis automatically applies. Regulatory relief is tied to the activity and factual record presented.

Canton is positioned for financial market applications where operators need clarity about how they can run validators and receive network rewards. An ambiguous securities treatment can affect procurement, legal review, custody and participation. Staff's response may remove one element of uncertainty for the described activities, but other obligations remain. Broker-dealer, banking, sanctions, AML and derivatives rules may still matter depending on how an institution uses the network. The letter does not approve every financial product built on Canton or override separate laws that govern securities and financial intermediaries.

Other blockchain teams may study the letter because it explains which decentralization and utility features mattered to staff. Yet copying a token's terminology or validator labels will not reproduce its underlying facts. The better question is whether control, incentives, operational independence and launch history match the reasons the agency gave. The timing also matters: the SEC's March 2026 interpretation and November staff response form part of an evolving regulatory framework, so subsequent formal rulemaking, litigation or legislative action could change the practical picture.

Developers and investors should read the response and the underlying request together, then follow any further SEC guidance affecting digital commodities and token rewards. One should also watch how institutions actually participate, including custody arrangements and the distribution of validator control. Stronger regulatory clarity can encourage experimentation, but it does not guarantee token liquidity, network security or an investment return. The precise achievement here is a fact-specific assurance about specified activities, not an open-ended licence for tokenization.

Zcash has set a new high in its network hashrate just days after the NU7 upgrade, which slashed block times by a third to 25 seconds. Zcash activated its NU7 upgrade on November 6, 2026, at block 3,543,405.

Zcash network hashrate: 32.62 GSol/s, up 5.8% in 30 days. ⛏️ An all-time high. https://t.co/1vNROBAvd2

Zcash hashrate refers to the total computing power of all miners on the ZEC network. It is calculated by the current network difficulty, the average block find time set by the cryptocurrency network and/or the effective block find time of the latest blocks.

ZEC got 3x faster following the NU7 upgrade, which launched on November 6, with block times down from 75 to 25 seconds, and the Sprout pool retired, marking a new era for Zcash.

Faster blocks mean more room for shielded transactions. NU7 adds per-block limits: 330 Orchard or Ironwood actions, 300 Sapling inputs and outputs, a shared budget of 330 across pools, and no new Sprout JoinSplits. These limits more than double Orchard protocol throughput while reducing the worst-case sync load a spammer can push onto light wallets by about 37%.

NU7 does not raise Zcash's fixed 21 million cap; halvings will now come every 5,040,000 blocks instead of 1,680,000, so the issuance schedule holds at roughly four years per halving. NU7 also starts allocating funds for future mining rewards. Some 60% of aggregate transaction fees will flow into a public reserve that pays later mining rewards.

In what comes next after the NU7 upgrade, Zcash developers have proposed cutting block times in a potential NU7.1 upgrade just days after NU7 went live. The proposal would reduce target block times from 25 to 20 seconds, aiming to speed up transaction confirmations and improve user experience and network latency.

The reaction of the S&P 500 suggested buyer strength, which could translate into strong crypto demand later, during the New York session open.

AMBCrypto reported that Bitcoin prices had fallen below the true market mean at $77.6k recently. Now, it was also trading below the 50-week Moving Average (MA).

Head of Research at Galaxy, Alex Thorn, pointed out that BTC has only slipped below its 50-week MA twice, after reclaiming it as a post-bear bottom. In neither of those times, which were in 2012 and 2019-20, did BTC descend to new weekly lows.

At the time of writing, the momentum was bearish, and a price drop below $70k was feasible. The $65k-$66k area would represent a deep discount opportunity for buyers. In the coming days, more losses appeared likely.

#5203. Canton Hosts Tokenized US Share Trade Under SEC Innovation Exemption

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: A tokenized share transaction involving a Nasdaq-listed company has taken place on Canton under a US regulatory exemption, according to an announcement from venue operator TSV. The November 4 transaction involved shares of Canton Strategic Holdings and a permissioned pool using Tradecraft's automated market maker technology.

A tokenized share transaction involving a Nasdaq-listed company has taken place on Canton under a US regulatory exemption, according to an announcement from venue operator TSV. The November 4 transaction involved shares of Canton Strategic Holdings and a permissioned pool using Tradecraft's automated market maker technology. The important development is not that a stock price was mirrored on a blockchain, but that the transaction was structured around the issuer, a transfer agent and verified holders.

TSV says DRW Cumberland purchased tokenized Canton Strategic Holdings common stock from existing shareholder Five North. Fairmint, an SEC-registered transfer agent, recorded the shares in token form in a verified wallet, and Flowdesk provided liquidity. The parties describe this as the first trade of its kind under the SEC's innovation exemption. Because this is an operator announcement, the scope of that first-of-kind claim should be attributed to the participants. What can be identified concretely is the named issuer, the parties, the permissioned environment and the transfer-agent role in the share record.

Tokenized equities can describe several very different products. Some are economic exposures issued by a separate intermediary; others aim to represent the issuer's shares with the rights and recordkeeping attached to conventional stock. Here the issuer-sponsored structure and transfer-agent involvement are central. They are intended to connect token holdings with the legally recognized ownership register, rather than just a derivative tracking a market price. Investors still need to know transfer restrictions, voting rights, eligibility rules and how corporate actions are administered. A blockchain token is not proof of all those protections by itself.

The reported transactions occurred in a permissioned pool with verified participants. That is fundamentally different from announcing that any wallet can buy US shares without checks or through a decentralized exchange. Restricted access may be a design choice needed to satisfy securities obligations, investor eligibility and transfer controls. It may also limit liquidity and interoperability compared with the open token markets crypto users are accustomed to. The test of such infrastructure is whether these controls can function at scale without making trading and settlement more cumbersome than conventional systems.

The company referred to an SEC innovation exemption announced in September. The transaction should be read within the specific conditions of the applicable relief, not as proof the SEC has deregulated all tokenized securities. Different venues, issuers or instruments may require their own legal analysis. Reporting on this area is especially sensitive to the distinction between an operational pilot, a live limited transaction and a broadly available retail market. This appears to be the second category: a real transaction, but with explicit participation boundaries.

Future announcements should reveal the number and variety of issuers, whether transactions settle consistently, how ownership and voting are handled, and whether participants can transfer positions between approved venues. Costs, order-book depth and operational incidents will be more revealing than another first-trade headline. If tokenized US equities become a durable market structure, those unglamorous details will matter at least as much as the chain carrying the record.

Primary source: Tradecraft / TSV official announcement. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s earlier report on transfer agents supporting tokenized securities.

Bitcoin (BTC) price dropped 1.9% over the past 24 hours on Monday, to trade near $74,239, breaking below the psychologically critical $75,000 mark. The decline brings the $74,400 support level into sharp focus as traders weigh the risk of a deeper market correction.

#5200. Ethereum (ETH) Gas Estimates Are Broken: Explaining the Fix and the Issue

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Ethereum transactions can appear successful, but there might be a problem hiding behind the scenes.

A Geth developer has proposed a fix to the client's gas estimation, according to draft pull request #36084 on GitHub. The patch addresses an issue in the current estimator, which could result in incorrect gas limits due to failed internal calls (calls from one smart contract to another) being ignored.

Although the transaction could still be completed, there is no evidence that the action the user wanted has actually happened.

The issue lies in a mechanism where a smart contract calls another smart contract, catches an error, and then proceeds to a refund, records the failure, or skips an item entirely. Technically, the transaction was successful, but the outcome is different for the user.

This could potentially result in wallets suggesting a gas limit that is enough to finish the transaction, but not enough to complete the work inside it. The developer also noted that EIP-8037 could make this behavior more common, since gas returned from failed internal execution can help fund the fallback.

According to the pull request, the change includes a stricter definition of success for gas estimates. This version of Geth would improve the way it deals with internal failures, counting failed internal calls and contract creations instead of checking only whether the transaction completes.

Even if the transaction completes, the estimate would get rejected if it produces more internal failures than a reference execution with a higher gas limit.

Nonetheless, the developer stressed that an internal call that always fails should not push the estimate higher indefinitely. The reference execution enables the estimator to keep existing failures without allowing additional ones caused by insufficient gas. The proposal also introduces a separate Amsterdam reference, preventing unnecessary increases made purely to access the state gas reservoir.

The developer states that they've replayed 432 mainnet transactions with the new set of rules from the Amsterdam update and that the suggested change fixed 64 out of 67 cases.

The gas limit increased by 4%. 254 additional estimates were unaffected due to the lack of the problem, with 3 cases being undetected.

For regular investors, the proposed change should improve the reliability of wallet estimates and reduce transactions that complete without delivering the intended result, despite introducing higher gas limits in some cases. Luckily, there is no proven link between higher gas limits and higher fees.

#5199. Broadridge Says Blockchain Repo Platform Processed $7.6T in October

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Broadridge says its Distributed Ledger Repo service processed $7.6 trillion in repurchase agreement transactions during October, averaging $345 billion a day. The November 6 disclosure is a striking reminder that some of blockchain's largest financial use cases are institutional plumbing rather than publicly traded tokens.

Broadridge says its Distributed Ledger Repo service processed $7.6 trillion in repurchase agreement transactions during October, averaging $345 billion a day. The November 6 disclosure is a striking reminder that some of blockchain's largest financial use cases are institutional plumbing rather than publicly traded tokens. It also needs context: a month of cumulative repo activity is a flow measure, not $7.6 trillion of newly created blockchain assets.

Repurchase agreements are short-term financing arrangements in which securities are sold with an agreement to repurchase them, often against cash collateral. They are a major part of the funding market for banks and dealers. Broadridge's figure represents cumulative transaction processing through its DLR system during October, while the average daily figure gives a sense of ongoing throughput. It should not be mistaken for assets permanently locked in a protocol or a standalone market capitalization. Repeated financing transactions can generate large summed volume even while the underlying collateral turns over.

Repo involves collateral records, cash movement, timing, reconciliations and multiple operational teams. A shared transaction environment can reduce disagreements about the state of a deal and help participants coordinate settlement. That is an attractive use case for distributed infrastructure precisely because the counterparties may already be regulated financial institutions that need detailed permissions and controls. Broadridge's announcement presents DLR as a production platform, rather than a proof of concept. Still, the release does not by itself quantify net cost savings for individual users or independently verify every reported operational benefit.

Broadridge is using the DLR experience to promote its DLX platform, which it says supports issuance, trading, settlement, financing and asset servicing. This is a commercial strategy to connect workflows that are currently separate. A tokenized asset is more useful if it can be financed, transferred, serviced and reported without expensive custom integrations. The difficulty is coordination with existing custody, legal rights and market infrastructure. Moving one record onchain does not magically resolve differences between firms' processes, and institutional adoption may continue to favor permissioned arrangements.

The October number suggests substantial existing demand for shared-ledger settlement in securities financing. It does not mean all traditional repo has moved onto a blockchain, nor does it imply that users can trade the underlying collateral publicly. Differences between tokenized records, ownership registers and conventional settlement obligations can be legally significant. Readers should look for comparable periods, the number and diversity of participating institutions, operational resilience and the share of transactions that run without manual intervention. Those indicators help distinguish a very large gross number from lasting efficiency gains.

Broadridge expects tokenized finance to extend further through normal market operations in 2027. The most revealing milestones will be independent institutional adoption and recurring transaction volume across multiple product types. For crypto investors, the lesson is to separate blockchain use as infrastructure from token speculation. A huge processing volume can demonstrate a serious enterprise application without creating direct demand for a liquid crypto token.

#5198. Binance to shut down its Bitcoin mining pool – Despite $233M in Q3 revenue

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Binance is set to shut down its Bitcoin [BTC] mining pool on the 10th of November. However, the decision in no sense means the crypto exchange is exiting Bitcoin mining altogether.

Launched in April 2020, Binane pool allowed independent miners to combine their computing power and receive more predictable mining rewards. However, its influence has gradually diminished.

According to data by mempool.space, Binance [BNB] Pool’s hashrate index fell from approximately 26 exahashes per second (EH/s) in December 2025 to 9.2 EH/s in October 2026.

In other words, there was a decline of roughly 65%, taking its estimated share of Bitcoin’s network hashrate from 2.3% to less than 1%.

At the same time, Binance Pool mined just one block in the seven-day period, representing approximately 0.11% of the 925 blocks discovered across the Bitcoin network. In fact, it recorded zero blocks in the latest 24 hours.

However, to date it has mined 22,213 blocks, accounting for approximately 2.28% of all Bitcoin blocks.

This comes as there is also a broader economic challenge facing the Bitcoin mining industry. Following the April 2024 halving, the block subsidy dropped from 6.25 BTC to 3.125 BTC, reducing the amount of newly issued Bitcoin miners receive for producing blocks.

Meanwhile, competitors including Foundry USA, AntPool, and F2Pool have become particularly dominant, together accounting for a substantial share of recent Bitcoin block discoveries.

Another important factor is the changing direction of the broader mining industry. Several publicly traded Bitcoin miners have started exploring artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure as alternative revenue sources.

Lastly, Bitcoin miner outflows were also fluctuating throughout 2026, with most daily readings remaining between 5,000 and 10,000 BTC.

However, November 2026 is notable for the absence of a sustained surge in selling activity. Daily outflows have mostly remained moderate, with the index standing at 6,800 BTC at press time.

At the same time, Bitcoin’s price has weakened from around $80,000 in late October to approximately $74,200 at press time.

Together, these figures strongly suggest that Binance Pool’s mining activity had fallen considerably ahead of its scheduled November 10 shutdown.

Besides this, Core Scientific, once the largest Bitcoin [BTC] miner, also announced its plans to shut down its Bitcoin mining by Q4 2026 despite Q3 revenue hitting $233 million.

#5195. Dinari Adds Broadridge Voting Rails to Tokenized US Shares

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Tokenized stocks have often promised easier access and faster settlement, but a less glamorous question keeps surfacing: can the holder vote? Broadridge and Dinari announced an integration on November 5 that aims to connect eligible holders of Dinari's dShares to established proxy-voting infrastructure.

Tokenized stocks have often promised easier access and faster settlement, but a less glamorous question keeps surfacing: can the holder vote? Broadridge and Dinari announced an integration on November 5 that aims to connect eligible holders of Dinari's dShares to established proxy-voting infrastructure. The development highlights shareholder governance as a core feature of credible tokenization, not an optional extra on a trading app.

According to the companies, eligible dShare holders can exercise voting rights associated with the underlying US equities through Broadridge's proxy systems. Those votes are intended to enter the same formal processes used by traditional shareholders. This is more concrete than giving token holders a separate community poll about a company. Shareholder resolutions, board elections and other corporate actions depend on recognized ownership records, deadlines and entitlement calculations. The release describes an integration of these processes, although it does not publish a full end-to-end test record for each supported company.

A user buying exposure to a company's share may assume the resulting token comes with the same rights as a share in a conventional brokerage account. That assumption is dangerous unless the product's legal structure supports it. Some tokens are claims on intermediaries, while others are issued and serviced in ways designed to preserve shareholder entitlements. Dinari's integration addresses part of that problem by moving voting instructions through established channels. Investors should still verify which tokens qualify, whether voting is available in their jurisdiction and how any intermediary custody arrangements affect their position.

Broadridge already handles a large volume of investor communications and governance workflows in traditional markets. Connecting these systems to a tokenized product can be more practical than reconstructing every corporate-action process from scratch. That matters because an issuer cannot simply ignore events such as stock splits, tender offers or changes in the shareholder register. There may also be timing conflicts between token transfer windows and voting record dates. The harder task is keeping balances, entitlements and instruction chains aligned as holders move between wallets and supported intermediaries.

An improved voting experience does not automatically make a tokenized share freely transferable, exchange-listed or protected identically in every jurisdiction. Eligibility, investor verification and local securities rules may still apply. Likewise, a voting feature says little about trading liquidity or the robustness of the underlying custody model. Broadridge and Dinari's announcement is best understood as one part of the market's operational maturation. It makes a necessary ownership function more visible, but cannot settle every legal or commercial question around tokenized equities.

Useful evidence would include the number of supported issuers, actual voting participation by eligible holders, records of successful proxy delivery and support for other corporate actions. For asset managers and platforms considering tokenized stock distribution, governance infrastructure is a test of whether the product behaves like an investment or merely tracks its price. That distinction will become more important as institutions offer these instruments to a broader audience.

#5194. Ethereum loses 2024 gains – Is Vitalik Buterin rethinking ETH’s long-term value?

Ethereum’s [ETH] long-term investment case has been relatively weaker compared to Bitcoin.

On an annual basis, ETH has fallen nearly 30% this year, dragging its price down to $1.5k levels, and eliminating all the gains made throughout 2024 and 2025. What’s more, the altcoin is currently trading nearly 10% “lower” than it was at the start of 2024, highlighting its weak cycle-wide returns.

Bitcoin, on the other hand, has been much more resilient. After correcting 15% in 2026, BTC is still trading above 75% higher from its 2024 starting point, representing a much better long term ROI. The weakness extends into the ETH/BTC ratio, which is down over 16%, heading towards a fifth consecutive bearish annual candle. The ratio also trades around 60% below its 2024 opening level.

In essence, Bitcoin has maintained a clear lead in the long-term investment narrative.

According to AMBCrypto, this is where Vitalik Buterin’s recent X post comes into play. For years, Ethereum’s investment thesis has revolved around its deflationary model, lower gas fees, and token-burn mechanics. The idea was to strengthen ETH’s value proposition through reduced supply and increased network activity.

However, ETH’s continued underperformance relative to BTC raises questions about how well this supply-driven narrative is translating into price action. In this light, Buterin’s new SOV thesis may be an attempt to drive this change in investment thesis. By highlighting Ethereumas a “store of value,” Buterin might be trying to shift ETH’s investment thesis to that of being a long-term value asset.

The reason behind Vitalik Buterin’s changing approach is becoming clearer from on-chain data.

According to on-chain data, ETH burns have declined by 98.8% from $3.548 billion in 2022 to just $42.8 million in 2026. This reduces how much of the Ethereum supply is being taken out of circulation, therefore undermining the deflationary narrative. This means the emphasis will shift to demand. Ethereum may derive more of its long-term value from becoming a collateral rather than from supply reduction through token burns.

Against this backdrop, recent whale activity adds another layer to ETH’s outlook. According to Onchain Lens, a large holder has withdrawn 16,580 ETH from Binance. However, whale accumulation might not be enough to compensate for a lack of staking demand. According to ValidatorQueue, the amount of ETH waiting to be staked has been on a downtrend since peaking at 4 million ETH in February.

This is where Buterin’s new store-of-value (SOV) narrative becomes important.

With staking demand declining, Ethereum’s collateral use case could also come under pressure. As ETH acts as collateral for loans, DeFi positions and overall financial activity within the ecosystem, a continued decrease in demand to hold and use ETH as collateral could put downward pressure on its long-term utility.

From this perspective, Vitalik Buterin’s latest post could be a key moment in reshaping Ethereum’s long-term investment case against Bitcoin.

Cardano (ADA) has entered epoch 666, yet another milestone for the blockchain, which has been live since its launch in September 2017.

The number has drawn attention for its connection to the biblical 666, but the development also points to the Cardano network's basic timekeeping and staking mechanism.

Popular Cardano blockchain explorer Cexplorer displays that epoch 666 started on Nov. 5, 2026, and is expected to end on Nov. 10, with 1 day and 10 hours left to close. The milestone marks another five-day cycle finished in Cardano's long-running proof-of-stake system.

Cardano divides its operation into epochs, which are five days long and consist of 432,000 one-second slots. The importance of epoch 666 is largely symbolic and not technical, as it does not coincide with any major protocol upgrades or hard forks. But the number 666 has merely provided an interesting talking point for the Cardano community.

In a separate milestone, the Cardano network has processed over 127,000,000 transactions on mainnet. According to Cexplorer data, Cardano has recorded a total of 127,203,164 transactions.

In upgrade news, DijkstraNet, the Dijkstra hard fork testnet, has been hard forked to protocol version 12 and is now available for testing and integration against the full Dijkstra feature set, with the exception of Linear Leios.

Node 11.2 was pre-released on October 28 and successfully used to transition DijkstraNet into the Dijkstra era, and DB Sync 13.8.0.0 was released for all networks.

In separate upgrade news, Midnight has completed its upgrade from Ledger 8 to Ledger 9, bringing new capabilities for developers alongside security, compatibility, and performance improvements across the network.

Ledger 9 introduces native support for widely used cryptographic standards including ECDSA and Keccak-256, expands wallet and custody compatibility, and enables contracts to interact directly with one another.

Keccak-256 is the standard algorithm that Ethereum uses to scramble data into fixed-length cryptographic fingerprints. ECDSA is the standard digital signature method that networks like Bitcoin and Ethereum use to prove ownership of a specific wallet address.

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

TL;DR: Ondo Finance says its tokenized real-world-asset products have crossed $4 billion in value, with 484 distinct assets and more than 565,000 onchain holders. The figures appear in a corrected November 5 company announcement citing RWA.xyz data.

Ondo Finance says its tokenized real-world-asset products have crossed $4 billion in value, with 484 distinct assets and more than 565,000 onchain holders. The figures appear in a corrected November 5 company announcement citing RWA.xyz data. They illustrate how tokenized finance is broadening beyond a small set of Treasury products, but the definitions behind a ranking matter as much as the impressive headline figure.

The corrected release says Ondo ranks first among 203 platforms tracked by RWA.xyz by the market capitalization of tokenized products and accounts for roughly a tenth of non-stablecoin RWA value. The comparison excludes stablecoins and uses the data provider's classification of assets and platforms. Readers should not confuse it with Ondo's revenue, cash on its balance sheet, net inflows in a single day or the trading volume of the ONDO token. Tokenized product value can also move with prices and redemptions, so the number should be treated as a dated snapshot rather than an immutable milestone.

The category now spans short-term government debt, funds, equities and other exposures offered through various legal and custody structures. Those instruments may all be called real-world assets while providing very different rights, liquidity and redemption procedures. A tokenized money market interest can behave unlike a tokenized stock, and neither should be analyzed simply as an unsecured crypto token. The key question is what claim the holder owns, who maintains the legal records and how a user receives the underlying value when a transaction or redemption is requested.

Issuing a blockchain representation is relatively straightforward compared with making it useful to investors and institutions. Platforms need identity checks, compliant distribution, secondary transfer controls, custody arrangements and ongoing servicing. The scale reported by Ondo suggests that these practical layers have become commercially significant. Yet a large holder count does not disclose how assets are concentrated, whether addresses represent individuals or intermediaries, or what proportion trades regularly. A platform can be large by outstanding value while some products remain relatively illiquid.

Ondo issued this information as a correction, making it particularly important to use the complete revised text rather than an earlier headline copied across aggregators. Rankings also depend on the measurement date and definitions used by the data provider. A later expansion of coverage or reclassification could change relative positions without any shift in underlying user demand. Readers should therefore seek source methodology and product-level information before interpreting a top ranking as evidence of an uncontested or permanent market lead.

The strongest sign of maturation will be whether tokenized products are used in ordinary financial workflows: collateral management, settlement, portfolio allocation and redemptions. Transparent asset backing, enforceable rights and resilient operations will matter more than product count alone. Ondo's milestone is a useful indicator of scale, provided it is presented as a company-reported snapshot of tokenized assets rather than a promise about future returns or market dominance.

TL;DR: Schroders is bringing an emerging-market bond strategy into the tokenized fund market through Centrifuge on Solana. The November 4 announcement concerns the Schroder International Selection Fund Emerging Market Bond strategy, with Centrifuge providing onchain infrastructure.

Schroders is bringing an emerging-market bond strategy into the tokenized fund market through Centrifuge on Solana. The November 4 announcement concerns the Schroder International Selection Fund Emerging Market Bond strategy, with Centrifuge providing onchain infrastructure. It is notable because the assets are not a cryptocurrency basket: investors are being offered a blockchain-native route to a conventional, actively managed fixed-income strategy with its own risks and investment processes.

Centrifuge says the initiative will introduce tokenized exposure to the Schroders emerging-market bond fund. Schroders manages more than $1 trillion in assets across its business, according to the announcement, and has decades of experience investing in debt issued by emerging-market governments and companies. That corporate scale provides context for the partnership; it is not an estimate of how much capital has entered this particular onchain fund. The launch represents Schroders' first Solana deployment, a specific milestone that should not be confused with a wholesale shift of the manager's portfolios to public blockchains.

Emerging-market bonds can offer access to currencies, credit risks and interest-rate conditions very different from those facing US Treasury bills. The underlying portfolio may be affected by sovereign finances, corporate defaults, currency movements and changes in global borrowing costs. Tokenization does not eliminate those exposures. It changes how interests in an investment strategy can be issued, recorded, distributed or serviced. Investors need to understand the fund's legal structure, eligibility, fees, dealing arrangements and the precise way token holdings map to recognized ownership. Those details ultimately determine whether the product meets their requirements.

Solana's appeal to financial product developers includes its transaction throughput and low per-transaction fees, while Centrifuge focuses on the specialist infrastructure needed to operate tokenized funds. The challenge is making asset management routines work with a public network without losing compliance controls. Fund subscriptions, redemptions, transfer restrictions and investor records must align with the legally constituted vehicle. A fast chain is helpful, but it cannot replace the fund administrator, custodian or manager. Operational success depends on the quality of those connections, not simply on the number of transactions the blockchain can process.

Much of the early RWA market concentrated on tokenized cash and short-dated US government debt. An actively managed emerging-market bond strategy is a different proposition because valuation, liquidity and portfolio turnover can be more complicated. A market may be open at all hours even when underlying bonds trade within narrower windows. That difference makes pricing and redemption policies essential. The value proposition could be broader distribution and improved processing, but investors should not infer that every share can be redeemed instantly or that tokenization creates round-the-clock liquidity in the underlying securities.

The next useful evidence would include an initial live issuance, assets held in the tokenized structure, participating distributors, supported jurisdictions and how subscriptions and redemptions actually settle. Over time, the question is whether blockchain infrastructure improves operational efficiency and attracts new investors without weakening fund protections. The announcement is a meaningful institutional experiment, but the practical success of the fund will rest on ordinary asset-management disciplines as much as on Solana technology.

#5187. Bybit Expands RWA Earn Into Japanese Equities With New JPE Product

Home » Crypto Market News » Bybit Expands RWA Earn Into Japanese Equities With New JPE Product

Bybit’s first equity product in RWA Earn gives access to an SBI Asset Management strategy.

Bybit is expanding its RWA Earn platform into Japanese equities with the launch of JPE, its first equity-based investment product.

Announced on November 9, the product marks the platform’s first equity offering and gives eligible users indirect exposure to a Japanese high-dividend equity strategy managed by SBI Asset Management (SBI AM).

The launch brings a new asset class to Bybit RWA Earn, which previously focused on fixed-income and credit strategies.

According to an official announcement, the JPE investment product will give eligible Bybit users indirect exposure to a Japanese high-dividend equity strategy managed by SBI Asset Management (SBI AM).

JPE is backed by JX, a digital token issued by DigiFT, a platform specializing in tokenized traditional investments.

Plume, a blockchain-based financial infrastructure provider, structures the product for distribution through Bybit’s RWA Earn platform. The underlying Japanese equity strategy remains managed by SBI Asset Management.

Bybit said eligible users can invest in JPE through its RWA Earn platform using USDC, with a minimum subscription of 5,000 USDC.

The exchange will cover all blockchain transaction fees, while subscriptions and redemptions will be free of charge. Redemptions will follow a T+5 settlement cycle, excluding non-trading days in Japan, Singapore and the United States.

Emily Bao, Bybit’s Head of Spot & Assets, said the launch reflects the growing role of partnerships in bringing traditional financial assets onto blockchain networks. She added that the collaboration with Plume and DigiFT allows Bybit to offer users access to institutional-grade investment products backed by established asset managers.

Full details, restricted regions and eligibility criteria are available in Bybit’s official announcement.

The launch marks an expansion of Bybit’s RWA offering into traditional equity markets.

Since its launch in June 2026, Bybit RWA Earn has focused on tokenized fixed-income and credit products, giving eligible users access to investment strategies beyond crypto-native assets.

With the addition of JPE, the platform is moving into equities for the first time, offering indirect exposure to a Japanese high-dividend equity strategy managed by SBI Asset Management.

The global real-world asset (RWA) market reached $39.61 billion in distributed asset value as of November 8, according to RWA.xyz, down 0.94% over the previous 30 days. The value of represented assets stood at $391.90 billion, up 8.87%. The market had around 5.69 million asset holders, an increase of 7.13% over the same period.

U.S. Treasury debt remained the largest RWA category, with $14.11 billion in distributed value, followed by commodities at $5.33 billion and active strategies at $4.72 billion. Tokenized stocks ranked among the larger categories, reaching approximately $3.73 billion.

Tokenized equities are moving from fixed income into stock-based strategies on Bybit exchange. It also gives eligible investors access to a Japanese high-dividend equity strategy through a blockchain-based product.

#5184. Nigeria tells dollar-stablecoin issuers: go local or lose retail access

Retail dollar stablecoins need Nigerian issuers, local licenses and token approval. Existing operators need express interim permission during the transition.

Nigeria’s central bank now requires dollar-pegged stablecoins offered to retail customers to be issued by locally incorporated, licensed entities and receive token approval. The rules took effect November 5, 2026, with a conditional 180-day application transition for existing operators. Continued access for foreign-currency stablecoin arrangements during assessment requires express permission from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN).

The CBN regulations classify foreign-currency stablecoins as Class 2. Section 6.5 requires a Nigerian-incorporated entity holding a Foreign Currency Issuer License (Class 2), alongside approval of the token itself.

A foreign license, regulatory status or agreement with a Nigerian intermediary cannot substitute for those approvals. The rules reach regulated activities directed at people in Nigeria even when the provider has no physical presence there.

Issuers and service providers face distinct approval requirements. Non-issuance service licenses or authorizations do not permit stablecoin issuance, while issuer applicants must establish a staffed Nigerian office and effective local management before final licensing, including a resident chief compliance officer.

The framework makes a narrow exception to local issuance. Section 11.10.17 allows the CBN to recognize a foreign-issued stablecoin solely for expressly approved wholesale cross-border settlement. That route excludes offerings to Nigerian retail customers, so it does not provide a substitute for the retail licensing requirements.

Approval also has limits on domestic use. Class 2 Token Approval does not authorize settling, pricing or discharging a naira-denominated domestic obligation unless applicable foreign-exchange or other law expressly permits it.

The regulations preserve the Securities and Exchange Commission’s statutory jurisdiction and do not automatically cancel approvals under other Nigerian frameworks. An existing principal license nevertheless does not remove the need for express CBN approval for non-security virtual asset services.

Section 54.1 gives existing operators 180 calendar days from commencement to submit a complete application for the appropriate license or authorization. They may continue only at their existing scale and subject to the CBN’s interim conditions.

Submitting an application alone therefore does not establish permission to keep serving the market.
